source.excerpt: To love is to wish good to someone.
trail: In Summa Theologiae I–II, question 26, article 4, Aquinas introduces the definition as the Philosopher’s, citing Rhetoric II. The Vatican Catechism renders it “To love is to will the good of another.” The displayed “the other” is not the wording of either checked English source. The Summa argument ↗
The official English Catechism reads “To love is to will the good of another.” Catechism paragraph 1766 ↗

author.bio: Aquinas drew extensively on Aristotle while developing his account of human action and the passions. This passage belongs to his discussion of love, rather than an independent aphorism claiming a newly invented definition.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Aquinas introduces the definition by explicitly citing Aristotle. Modern English versions differ between wishing good to someone and willing the good of another, so the short familiar formulation needs both a translation qualification and an acknowledgment of the older source.

schema.faqAnswer: Aquinas quotes this definition from Aristotle in Summa Theologiae I–II, question 26, article 4. The checked English source says “to wish good to someone”; the displayed wording is a modern variant, not a newly coined Aquinas definition.
